newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PEKAO SA BANK LAUNCHES HOUSING LOANS SCHEME.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PEKAO SA BANK LAUNCHES HOUSING LOANS SCHEME.

text.p: Poland's state-owned Bank Pekao SA on Monday launched the country's first housing savings and loans scheme which offers low-interest loans for residential property in exchange for low-interest deposits.
Marian Czekanski, Pekao's deputy president, told a news conference that the scheme would earn profits for the bank if at least 15,000 people joined it every year.

Clients who keep their savings in the bank for at least three years in low-interest accounts paying 25 percent of the central bank's discount rate, now at 22 percent, will be eligible to take out a loan for housing at an interest rate 50 percent lower than the discount rate.
The clients will be able to borrow up to 1.5 times the deposited amount.

Pekao officials said the bank would charge a 1.8 percent commission on deposits and would retain a one-percent share of the scheme's eventual profits, while the balance of the profits would be ploughed back into the fund.

Construction minister Barbara Blida, also present, said the scheme allowed its participants to benefit from preferential tax treatment and take advantage of tax deductions for contributions to savings accounts.

But Pekao officials said its success would depend largely on how far-reaching the deductions would be and signalled that planned income tax changes for next year would limit the tax advantages of the system.
